groups.title: Oral Suspension (101330ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Ages 4 to 6 months: take 2.5 mL (80 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 7 to 23 months: take 3.5 mL (120 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 2 to 3 years: take 5 mL (160 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 4 to 6 years: take 7.5 mL (240 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 7 to 8 years: take 10 mL (320 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 9 to 10 years: take 12.5 mL (400 mg) as 1 dose. Age 11 years: take 15 mL (480 mg) as 1 dose. Age 12 years: take 20 mL (640 mg) as 1 dose. Take a dose every 4 to 6 hours when needed. If the body weight is known, dosing according to body weight is more appropriate. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg).
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine. Do not take it if you have phenylketonuria and need to restrict your intake of phenylalanine.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, reduced cardiac function or a bleeding tendency, or if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment, kidney impairment, a peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a bleeding tendency, abnormal heart function or hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are elderly; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Do not take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or another anti-inflammatory analgesic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic or flucloxacillin.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, reduced platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell syndrome), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E78400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoid symptoms that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 capsules as 1 dose, 1 time in 1 day at bedtime. Take the smallest amount for the first dose, then increase or reduce the amount gradually while checking the shape and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal condition such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis; if you have intestinal obstruction; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soya bean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya beans or peanuts.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 10 years or under; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; if you are a patient in whom lipid emulsions must be given with care; if you are at risk from fat overload; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 (sunset yellow FCF) or Food Yellow No. 203 (quinoline yellow WS).

If your constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not keep taking it for more than 1 week. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (C97900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D, B1, B2, B6 and C and zinc in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during the growth years and in old age, and for the prevention of poor development of bone and teeth and of rickets, and for neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), beriberi, eye strain, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of the whole body of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have hyperoxaluria (excretion of an excessive amount of oxalate in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment, low blood protein, gout or folate deficiency; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 or Food Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test values. If your symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cardiac glycoside, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), depressed central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell of the sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorder, indigestion, upper abdominal pain or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (113232APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic enteritis, acute and chronic diarrhoea, acute dysentery, and abnormal fermentation in the bowel due to various causes.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 g as 1 dose, 3 times in 1 day; take 4 g for the first dose. Infants and young children: take 1 g as 1 dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an inherited problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If your symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with ciprofloxacin, or with imipenem and cilastatin sodium.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A25000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules as 1 dose. Children aged 8 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 capsule as 1 dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are elderly, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the supervision of a guardian. It may cause drowsiness, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If your symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid, or if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis with fever, redness and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), signs of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D75800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets as 1 dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

In patients taking acetaminophen, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell syndrome), have very rarely been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more; or if you have an inherited problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have a constitution prone to contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are elderly, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not keep taking it for a long period.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have taken a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body or on the mouth or eye membranes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (199402ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhoea, bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, bruise, injury, low back and sacral pain), pain after surgery, migraine and pain after tooth extraction.
groups.usage: Adults, for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: take 1 to 2 capsules (250 to 500 mg) as 1 dose, 2 times in 1 day (every 12 hours). For acute gout: take 3 capsules (750 mg) as the first dose, then take 1 capsule (250 mg) every 8 hours until the attack subsides. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis: take 2 capsules (500 mg) as the first dose, then take 1 capsule (250 mg) every 6 to 8 hours, and do not exceed a total of 5 capsules (1250 mg) in 1 day. For migraine: take 3 capsules (750 mg) as the first dose, and if needed take 1 to 2 more capsules (250 to 500 mg) in 1 day, 30 minutes after the first dose, and do not exceed a total of 5 capsules (1250 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. Serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract, which may be fatal, may occur while taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, to aspirin or to another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if you have a peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac failure, severe high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; if you have pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if the user is a baby aged 2 years or under.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you may be pregnant; if the user is a child; if you are elderly; if you have had a peptic ulcer; if you have a blood disorder or a bleeding tendency; if you have liver impairment, kidney impairment, impaired heart function or high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; or if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD).

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or a naproxen derivative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a hydantoin antiepileptic, a sulfonamide, a sulfonylurea blood-glucose-lowering medicine, propranolol or another beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor (captopril and the like), a loop or thiazide diuretic, probenecid, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), zidovudine or a new quinolone antibiotic (enoxacin and the like).

If, rarely, signs of shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, slow pulse, cold sweat, oedema and the like) or PIE syndrome (pulmonary infiltration with eosinophilia: fever, wheezing and the like) occurs, or if stomach discomfort, stomach pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, heartburn, diarrhoea, constipation, stomatitis, or, rarely, abdominal bloating, black stools, dry mouth, raised GOT or GPT, jaundice, hepatitis, kidney impairment, glomerulonephritis, blood in the urine, high potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, protein in the urine or renal failure occurs, or if drowsiness, impaired cognitive function, or, rarely, dizziness, headache, numbness of the hands and feet, reduced libido, fatigue, depression, abnormal dreams, loss of concentration, disorientation, insomnia, muscle pain, muscle weakness, tinnitus, hearing impairment or visual disturbance occurs, or if oedema, difficulty breathing, or, rarely, palpitations, myasthenia, congestive heart failure, eosinophilic pneumonia, an anaphylactoid reaction, a menstrual disorder, chills and fever, vasculitis, high blood sugar or low blood sugar occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults, for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: take 1 to 2 tablets (275 to 550 mg) as 1 dose, 2 times in 1 day (every 12 hours). For acute gout: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose, then take 1 tablet (275 mg) every 8 hours until the attack subsides. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis: take 2 tablets (550 mg) as the first dose, then take 1 tablet (275 mg) every 6 to 8 hours, and do not exceed a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day. For migraine: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose, and if needed take 1 to 2 more tablets (275 to 550 mg) in 1 day, 30 minutes after the first dose. Do not exceed a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe cardiac failure, severe kidney impairment or severe high blood pressure; if you have hypersensitivity to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have had asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery; if you have an inherited problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child; if you are elderly; if you have had a peptic ulcer or a blood disorder; if you have a bleeding tendency; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have impaired heart function, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; or if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, a naproxen derivative, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a hydantoin antiepileptic, a sulfonamide, a sulfonylurea blood-glucose-lowering medicine, propranolol or another beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor (captopril and the like), a loop or thiazide diuretic, probenecid, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), zidovudine or a new quinolone antibiotic (enoxacin and the like).

If a blood disorder such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red blood cells) or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Stomach discomfort, stomach pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, heartburn, diarrhoea, constipation and stomatitis may occur at times, and, rarely, abdominal bloating, black stools, dry mouth, raised GOT and GPT values, jaundice, hepatitis, kidney impairment, nephritis, blood in the urine, high potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, protein in the urine, renal failure, tinnitus, hearing impairment, visual disturbance, swelling, difficulty breathing, palpitations, myasthenia, congestive heart failure, eosinophilic pneumonia, an anaphylactoid reaction, a menstrual disorder, chills and fever, vasculitis, high blood sugar or low blood sugar may occur.
